evidence.claim: The official presidential biography records Jair Bolsonaro's term in office as 01/01/2019 to 31/12/2022.
evidence.title: Biografia
evidence.excerpt: The official presidential biography records Jair Bolsonaro's term in office as 01/01/2019 to 31/12/2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government biography with explicit term dates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's office and term.
contrary_evidence: Biographical pages are favorable by design and omit controversy.

evidence.claim: The World Bank estimated that 30.7% of Brazil's population experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022, and said food prices rose 37.5% between end-2019 and end-2022.
evidence.title: Inflação de alimentos e insegurança alimentar no Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank estimated that 30.7% of Brazil's population experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022, and said food prices rose 37.5% between end-2019 and end-2022.
evidence.source_locator: Body text discussing 2022 food insecurity and prices
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank analysis is high-quality and explicitly links 2022 food insecurity to inflation and household welfare.
evidence.period_fit: Explicitly discusses 2022 conditions, with retrospective comparisons to 2019-2021.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly contextual, but relevant to policy because social protection and inflation responses during Bolsonaro's term affected household exposure.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes social-protection measures cushioned the worst pandemic-era losses.
The evidence does not isolate Bolsonaro from inherited pandemic effects.

evidence.claim: By mid-2022, annual inflation in Brazil was estimated at 13.9%, and food costs had risen 13.43% in the 12 months to August 2022.
evidence.title: Fighting against poverty: the impact of inflation on households’ purchasing power
evidence.excerpt: By mid-2022, annual inflation in Brazil was estimated at 13.9%, and food costs had risen 13.43% in the 12 months to August 2022.
evidence.source_locator: Opinion text / data paragraph on Brazil
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank staff commentary draws on contemporaneous price data and is directly tied to household welfare.
evidence.period_fit: Directly addresses 2022 price conditions, published in October 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual; reflects inflation that Bolsonaro's government tried to offset but did not fully control.
contrary_evidence: Nominal average labor incomes also rose, partly offsetting the shock.
The piece is analytic commentary, not a ruler-specific audit.

evidence.claim: Reuters estimated that Bolsonaro's 2022 election-year benefits and promises would cost R$273 billion in 2022-2023, with R$127.4 billion already approved and implemented.
evidence.title: SAIBA MAIS-Benefícios em série e promessas de Bolsonaro em ano eleitoral têm custo de R$273 bi em 2022 e 2023
evidence.excerpt: Reuters estimated that Bolsonaro's 2022 election-year benefits and promises would cost R$273 billion in 2022-2023, with R$127.4 billion already approved and implemented.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent source, and the UOL mirror preserves the original report and numbers.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to the election period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's election strategy and executive choices.
contrary_evidence: Some measures were already approved through Congress, not by executive fiat alone.
Short-term relief can be justified in inflationary periods, but fiscal sustainability is the counterpoint.

evidence.claim: The UNICEF study says more than 60% of Brazilians up to age 17 live in poverty, and that poverty is multidimensional, covering education, sanitation, water, food, housing, and information; it also says racial and regional inequalities remain severe.
evidence.title: Pobreza Multidimensional na Infância e Adolescência no Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The UNICEF study says more than 60% of Brazilians up to age 17 live in poverty, and that poverty is multidimensional, covering education, sanitation, water, food, housing, and information; it also says racial and regional inequalities remain severe.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF is a strong child-welfare monitor and the page explicitly summarizes the study's Brazil-wide findings from IBGE data.
evidence.period_fit: The study uses data extending through 2022 for some dimensions and is directly relevant to the Bolsonaro-to-Lula transition context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly contextual rather than uniquely attributable to Bolsonaro; it reflects inherited structural conditions and pandemic-era deterioration during his term.
contrary_evidence: This is a synthesis page, not a ruler-specific audit.
It does not isolate Bolsonaro from pandemic and subnational effects.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said 2 million children and adolescents aged 11 to 19 were not attending school in Brazil, equal to 11% of the survey sample, and linked the problem to child labor and learning difficulties.
evidence.title: Dois milhões de crianças e adolescentes de 11 a 19 anos não estão frequentando a escola no Brasil, alerta UNICEF
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said 2 million children and adolescents aged 11 to 19 were not attending school in Brazil, equal to 11% of the survey sample, and linked the problem to child labor and learning difficulties.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF is a credible independent source and the page reports a concrete 2022 survey result with a direct percentage.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual, but relevant to Bolsonaro-era human-development outcomes and the government's responsibility to respond.
contrary_evidence: The study identifies pandemic-era learning disruption and labor as major drivers, so attribution is partial.
It does not by itself show a specific Bolsonaro policy failure.

evidence.claim: The World Bank estimated that 30.7% of Brazil's population experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022, and projected poverty at about 24.3% for 2022 as labor-market recovery and Bolsa Família adjustments offset some losses.
evidence.title: Inflação de alimentos e insegurança alimentar no Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank estimated that 30.7% of Brazil's population experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022, and projected poverty at about 24.3% for 2022 as labor-market recovery and Bolsa Família adjustments offset some losses.
evidence.source_locator: Body text on food insecurity, poverty, and labor-market recovery
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank analysis is high-quality and directly quantifies 2022 household hardship and the role of cash transfers.
evidence.period_fit: Explicitly discusses 2022 conditions, with some projections made during the year and retrospective comparisons to 2019-2021.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly contextual, but relevant because social-protection design and inflation response during Bolsonaro's administration affected household exposure.
contrary_evidence: The note also says labor-market recovery helped and that transfer programs cushioned losses.
It does not isolate Bolsonaro from inherited pandemic effects or global food shocks.

evidence.claim: The government said about 500,000 poor or extremely poor families were added to Auxílio Brasil in October 2022, bringing coverage to 21.1 million families and guaranteeing a minimum payment of R$600 per family.
evidence.title: Quase 500 mil famílias passam a integrar o programa Auxílio Brasil em outubro
evidence.excerpt: The government said about 500,000 poor or extremely poor families were added to Auxílio Brasil in October 2022, bringing coverage to 21.1 million families and guaranteeing a minimum payment of R$600 per family.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official program announcement with a clear beneficiary count and benefit floor.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Bolsonaro administration's cash-transfer policy and election-year execution, though some components were congressional or constitutional in origin.
contrary_evidence: The announcement is a policy claim, not an independent outcome evaluation.
The expansion also had an obvious election-year political dimension.

evidence.claim: The decree assigns health and education ministries responsibility for tracking Auxílio Brasil conditionalities, requires information sharing with the Ministry of Citizenship, and provides for social-assistance priority and review when families miss conditions.
evidence.title: D10852
evidence.excerpt: The decree assigns health and education ministries responsibility for tracking Auxílio Brasil conditionalities, requires information sharing with the Ministry of Citizenship, and provides for social-assistance priority and review when families miss conditions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary legal text with explicit operational rules for a national cash-transfer program.
evidence.period_fit: The decree text was in force during 2022 and directly governed that year’s program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential system design under Bolsonaro, though implementation depended on ministries and subnational networks.
contrary_evidence: Conditionalities do not prove high-quality delivery.
The text can exist even if enforcement is uneven.

evidence.claim: The ministry said the first 2022 education-conditionality monitoring period was discarded because of technical and operational inconsistencies in the school-presence system, and the resulting sanction was annulled.
evidence.title: Informe Auxílio Brasil 838
evidence.publisher: Ministério da Cidadania / Governo do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The ministry said the first 2022 education-conditionality monitoring period was discarded because of technical and operational inconsistencies in the school-presence system, and the resulting sanction was annulled.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is the direct administrative notice explaining a corrective action taken for the program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Bolsonaro-era welfare administration because it concerns program management and correction.
contrary_evidence: It also shows that the program's monitoring system had implementation problems.
A correction does not prove overall service quality.

evidence.claim: The government said Auxílio Brasil updated periodic data-verification rules to improve targeting by identifying discrepancies in family records against other federal databases.
evidence.title: Programa Auxílio Brasil atualiza os critérios de verificação de dados
evidence.excerpt: The government said Auxílio Brasil updated periodic data-verification rules to improve targeting by identifying discrepancies in family records against other federal databases.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official policy announcement describing a concrete administrative improvement to targeting and verification.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to the Bolsonaro administration's social-assistance management.
contrary_evidence: Targeting upgrades do not guarantee better outcomes on the ground.
This is process evidence, not a household-impact evaluation.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro signed a law creating Internet Brasil, a program to provide free mobile broadband to public-school students from CadÚnico families.
evidence.title: Governo Federal garante acesso à internet para alunos da rede pública
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro signed a law creating Internet Brasil, a program to provide free mobile broadband to public-school students from CadÚnico families.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official announcement of a signed law and the stated target population.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action, although implementation was shared with the communications and education ministries.
contrary_evidence: The page is promotional and does not measure take-up or learning gains.
Program creation is not the same as durable delivery.

evidence.claim: The decree regulates the internet-access program for public-school students and teachers, authorizing a one-time transfer of R$3.501 billion to states and the Federal District for educational internet access and requiring transparent distribution criteria.
evidence.title: D10952
evidence.excerpt: The decree regulates the internet-access program for public-school students and teachers, authorizing a one-time transfer of R$3.501 billion to states and the Federal District for educational internet access and requiring transparent distribution criteria.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary legal text with a specific budget amount and implementation conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's administration and its education-connectivity policy.
contrary_evidence: The transfer is still a delivery mechanism, not an outcome measure.
Actual access gains depended on state and municipal execution.

evidence.claim: Anatel approved a pilot to bring broadband internet to 177 public basic-education schools by March 2023 as part of a R$3.1 billion school-connectivity commitment.
evidence.title: Conselho Diretor aprova piloto para conectividade nas escolas
evidence.excerpt: Anatel approved a pilot to bring broadband internet to 177 public basic-education schools by March 2023 as part of a R$3.1 billion school-connectivity commitment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official regulator announcement with a concrete implementation milestone, though the commitment sits partly outside direct executive control.
evidence.period_fit: Late 2022 implementation context, with delivery extending into early 2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Bolsonaro-era policy design, but implementation was shared with regulators and telecom operators.
contrary_evidence: This is a pilot, not a full-system roll-out.
The funding came from telecom obligations, not only presidential spending choices.

evidence.claim: The health ministry launched a nationwide polio and multivaccination campaign aimed at vaccinating at least 95% of children aged 1 to under 5 against polio and updating vaccines for children and adolescents under 15.
evidence.title: Ministério da Saúde lança Campanha Nacional de Vacinação contra a Poliomielite e Multivacinação neste domingo (7)
evidence.excerpt: The health ministry launched a nationwide polio and multivaccination campaign aimed at vaccinating at least 95% of children aged 1 to under 5 against polio and updating vaccines for children and adolescents under 15.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry announcement with specific coverage targets and service scale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's government through the Ministry of Health, though campaign results are not shown on the page.
contrary_evidence: The announcement does not prove actual 95% coverage.
Vaccination campaigns were also responding to post-pandemic catch-up needs.

evidence.claim: The health ministry said Conitec favorably recommended incorporating Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine for children aged 6 months to under 5 years into the SUS.
evidence.title: Ministério da Saúde incorpora vacina Covid-19 para crianças de 6 meses a menores de 5 anos no SUS
evidence.excerpt: The health ministry said Conitec favorably recommended incorporating Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine for children aged 6 months to under 5 years into the SUS.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry notice reporting a formal incorporation recommendation for a vulnerable age group.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's health ministry decisions at the end of his term, though procurement and rollout were also constrained by technical processes.
contrary_evidence: This is a recommendation/incorporation notice rather than verified uptake.
It comes at the very end of the period.

evidence.claim: The ministry said that from 2019 to November 2022 it delivered more than 53 million primary-care attendances to indigenous peoples and that 20 health actions were carried out from 2020 to 2022 inside indigenous territories.
evidence.title: Assistência à população indígena foi uma das prioridades durante a pandemia de Covid-19; conheça as ações
evidence.excerpt: The ministry said that from 2019 to November 2022 it delivered more than 53 million primary-care attendances to indigenous peoples and that 20 health actions were carried out from 2020 to 2022 inside indigenous territories.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry report with specific service counts and a defined target population.
evidence.period_fit: Directly spans the Bolsonaro period through late 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's federal health administration, though the delivery depends heavily on specialized indigenous-health structures.
contrary_evidence: Official summaries can overstate effective quality or continuity of care.
The page does not independently verify health outcomes.

evidence.claim: The government expanded Casa Verde e Amarela financial support so urban households could receive up to R$130,000 and rural households up to R$55,000 for purchase, construction, or renovation.
evidence.title: Governo Federal amplia os limites do apoio financeiro do programa de habitação popular Casa Verde e Amarela
evidence.excerpt: The government expanded Casa Verde e Amarela financial support so urban households could receive up to R$130,000 and rural households up to R$55,000 for purchase, construction, or renovation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official announcement of a concrete change in housing support limits under a presidential decree.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action under Bolsonaro, though impacts on housing affordability depend on credit access and execution.
contrary_evidence: This is a financing ceiling, not a delivery result.
Housing support can still be unevenly distributed.

evidence.claim: IBGE says the 2022 census data let readers assess household living conditions through water supply, waste disposal, sewage, bathrooms, and piped water, and that the results are disaggregated by color/race and age groups.
evidence.title: Características dos domicílios - Resultados do Universo do Censo 2022
evidence.excerpt: IBGE says the 2022 census data let readers assess household living conditions through water supply, waste disposal, sewage, bathrooms, and piped water, and that the results are disaggregated by color/race and age groups.
evidence.source_locator: About - Characteristics of Housing Units / Results of the universe
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IBGE is the authoritative census source and the page describes the exact variables and disaggregation available for 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 census conditions, though published later.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual baseline rather than a ruler-specific policy result.
contrary_evidence: The page itself is a data-release description, not a welfare evaluation.
It does not isolate Bolsonaro-specific causal effects.

unresolved_gaps: Direct federal attribution for state-level police violence and Indigenous-harms response remains thinner than the adverse conduct record itself.
A direct Jair Bolsonaro asset-declaration, audit, or court-finding trail for 2022 self-dealing is still missing.
The original TSE-filed 2022 program is only indirectly represented here through a secondary summary.
Independent outcome audits for several flagship measures are still thinner than the implementation claims.

run_provenance.source_mix_note: Rich source metadata and chapter-specific reviewer exclusions were preserved during deterministic conversion.
